newsitem.title: FRANCE: Police, shop owners clash in France.
newsitem.headline: Police, shop owners clash in France.

text.p: French police fired tear gas on Monday in the southern city of Montpellier during clashes with several hundred people protesting at the detention of a right-wing shop owners' union leader suspected of sleaze.
About a dozen demonstrators were arrested, police said.

Several hundred members and sympathisers of the rightist Confederation for the Defence of Shop Owners and Artisans (CDCA) defied a local ban on street protests to urge the release of Christian Poucet, a CDCA leader held in preventive custody.

Police called on demonstrators to disperse before firing tear gas. Police initially arrested five protesters, but the detainees managed to break free with help from other demonstrators before police seized a new group.
Poucet was placed in preventive custody in Montpellier at the weekend on suspicion of failing to pay social security charges in a wider sleaze probe.
He is due to appear in court in Montpellier on Tuesday charged with making death threats against a magistrate. Poucet is also under investigation for illegal weapons possession.
